metadata.description: Single-plugin marketplace exposing the cc-enforcer discipline plugin.

plugins.name: cc-enforcer
plugins.description: Rules your coding agent physically cannot ignore. A Claude Code plugin (and LLM-agnostic rule pack) that stops reactive patching, guessed citations, surface-level fixes and premature "done" claims by intercepting the agent's own tool calls rather than asking it nicely. PreToolUse denies an edit before it lands — editing a file you never opened this session, a suppression marker with no adjacent why-comment, a hardcoded secret or user-home path, the fourth small patch to one file, a dangerous shell flag. A nine-layer Stop gate then refuses to let a completion claim end the turn without evidence, a convergence self-quiz, a fidelity check against the user's ORIGINAL request, and a one-line TL;DR. Twelve rules, eight backed by a hook; "Imperial Edict" regexes you define per project; a repo-wide sync gate; CI drift gates that derive every documented number from the code so the documentation cannot rot. Zero dependencies, stdlib only, Linux + Windows CI, and every guard fails OPEN — a bug in the discipline can never brick your agent. v0.35.1 is a documentation-truth release. The active half of rule 12 — the repo-refresh full-repo scan, unrun since v0.32.2 — found that both READMEs advertised a detector that does not exist: the layer-(b) row named "should be fine" and "应该" as hedges, the before/after demo was built on "Should be stable now", and the sample output claimed `Hedge matched: 'Should be'`. Bare `should` is deliberately excluded from the hedge set, as stop_guard's own comment states, so the demo's OUTPUT could not have come from its own INPUT — a plugin whose whole purpose is refusing unfounded claims was making one on its front page. v0.34.1 had aligned the injected PROMPTS down to the implementation and scoped that sweep to prompts/; the READMEs describe the same detector and were never in the sweep, so the class was closed on one surface and left open on another. Two siblings: the rolling-patch sample printed a per-file coverage bar of "1104 of 3672 chars" where lib/editscale computes 1102 (numbers a reader would take for captured output, written by hand), and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's Stop decision table cited HEDGED_DONE_REASON, NO_EVIDENCE_REASON, MISSING_QUIZ_REASON and MISSING_FIDELITY_REASON — four identifiers deleted in v0.12.0 and cited for the twenty-three releases since. Correcting the words would decay on the next release, so each class got a gate: hedge trigger examples derived from stop_guard._HEDGE_INNER, sample coverage bars from editscale.coverage_bar, and every backticked UPPER_SNAKE identifier in a non-CHANGELOG doc must resolve to a real definition or be registered as a doc-only exception with a reason. All three were verified RED against the pre-fix tree first, because a gate that only passes on fixed content cannot tell a working check from a deleted one. Two candidate findings were retracted during the same scan rather than shipped: a marketplace "mojibake" that was the terminal's cp936 rendering, and an AKIA "false negative" that was the documented placeholder hatch firing on a value containing EXAMPLE. This description was also trimmed from 18,496 characters: it had accumulated nine stacked release narratives duplicating CHANGELOG.md — the same second-source defect CLAUDE.md §6.1 diagnosed and fixed for itself. 676 -> 682 tests. Full release history: CHANGELOG.md.
